title: An Attitude It Can Trust: A Gyro for the Fast Part, the Accelerometer and the Feet for the Slow Part, and Which of Them Is Wrong When

questions.question: What is the gyro good for and bad for?
options: Good over a minute and noisy over a moment
Good over a moment and drifting over a minute, from its bias
Good while the body is still and useless once it walks
Good for roll and pitch, with no error that grows
questions.explanation: Adding up the rate adds up the bias with it. At 0.5 degrees per second the gyro alone was 23.1 degrees out after a minute.

questions.question: The accelerometer alone was wrong by how much in the walk?
options: 10.2 degrees (rms)
1.02 degrees (rms)
23.1 degrees (rms)
0.40 degrees (rms)
questions.explanation: The accelerometer cannot tell gravity from the body's own acceleration, and a walk shakes it by 2.5 m/s2 at every step.

questions.question: How much did the gate on the size of the acceleration reject?
options: About half, the readings taken while a foot was landing
Nearly all, which left too few readings to use
Only the readings more than 15 percent below g
Almost nothing: it accepted 100 percent, as a sideways shake barely changes the size
questions.explanation: Gravity with a sideways 2.5 m/s2 added has a size of 10.1, three percent above g, well inside a gate of 15 percent. The gate stops vertical jolts and lets through the shake that tilts the answer.

questions.question: With the feet as well, in a walk, the error was:
options: 1.02 degrees
10.2 degrees
0.40 degrees
Zero, since the feet do not drift
questions.explanation: The plane through three or more feet has no drift and no shake, so a second gentle pull toward it took the error from 1.02 to 0.40 degrees.

questions.question: Why can the feet not be used in a trot?
options: Their contact sense is too slow at a trot's pace
The legs' angles are not known during the swing
Only two are down, so there is no plane
The plane they give is shaken by the landing
questions.explanation: A plane needs three points. With two feet down there is only a line, so the filter is back to the gyro and the accelerometer: 1.02 degrees.

questions.question: What is not estimated?
options: The gyro's bias and the heading
The roll and the pitch
The pull toward the accelerometer
The feet's plane in a walk
questions.explanation: The filter leaves the bias in, which is where its steady error of about a degree comes from. Heading cannot come from gravity or from the feet at all.
